page: Amazon Web Services g4ad.16xlarge is a graphics-intensive server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running at 3.0 GHz, delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For accelerated workloads, the instance bundles four AMD Radeon Pro Navi V520 GPUs with a total of 32 GB VRAM. Local storage consists of 2400 GB of NVMe SSD, complemented by a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a mix of capabilities. Single-core CPU performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core and memory performance are robust, with the Passmark CPU score, extended instructions, and encryption tests all ranking in the top 25%. Geekbench ray tracing performance is also strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 57420.0. Large-model LLM inference presents a performance tradeoff; while prompt processing for a 70B model remains average, text generation for the same model drops to the bottom 25% at 2.73 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the g4ad.16xlarge offers a dense allocation of GPU resources and high-speed local NVMe storage relative to its compute profile, making it a viable option for graphics-intensive workloads without the premium associated with enterprise-grade deep learning accelerators. The instance is well-suited for ray tracing, image processing, multi-threaded decompression, and database operations. It is also appropriate for moderate LLM inference tasks using smaller models, though it is less optimal for single-threaded CPU-bound tasks or large-scale LLM text generation.
